title: Can you tell me where it is?
goal: Ask polite indirect questions with normal word order
intro: Polite questions often start with “Can you tell me…”, “Do you know…”, or “I wonder…”. After these openings, the second part goes back to normal statement order and loses do/does/did: “Can you tell me where the station is?” (not “where is the station”).

examples: Do you know what time it is?
Can you tell me where he lives?

rules.rule: Yes/no questions: use if or whether.
examples: Do you know if the shop is open?

rules.rule: Drop do/does/did in the second part.
examples: Could you tell me when the train leaves?
Do you know why he left?

mistakes.wrong: Can you tell me where is the bank?
mistakes.right: Can you tell me where the bank is?
mistakes.why: After “Can you tell me”, use statement order.

mistakes.wrong: Do you know what time does the film start?
mistakes.right: Do you know what time the film starts?

mistakes.wrong: I don’t know where did he go.
mistakes.right: I don’t know where he went.

mistakes.wrong: Can you tell me is he coming?
mistakes.right: Can you tell me if he is coming?

ex.q: Could you tell me what time ___?
I wonder ___ she got the job.
Can you tell me how much ___?
Do you know where does Priya live?
ex.fixed: Do you know where Priya lives?

ex.q: Can you tell me what is your name?
ex.fixed: Can you tell me what your name is?

ex.q: I don't know why did they cancel it.
ex.fixed: I don't know why they cancelled it.

ex.q: Do you know ___ the meeting is still on? (yes/no)

ex.a: Could you tell me where the lift is?

ex.q: Make it polite. Start with “Could you tell me”: “Where is the ATM?”
a: Could you tell me where the ATM is
ex.y: Statement order at the end: where the ATM is.

talk: You are in a new city. Ask the coach five polite questions starting with “Could you tell me…” or “Do you know…”.
